page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance balanced for mainstream computing workloads. Driven by the AMD EPYC 9B45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 virtual CPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512 vector operations, VNNI, bfloat16, and hardware cryptographic acceleration.

The compute profile is paired with 16 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is not bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached persistent disk volumes for secondary storage, and no hardware GPU acceleration is included. Benchmark measurements show top-tier single-threaded compute throughput, reflected in leading results across stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core execution.

Multithreaded metrics fall in the midrange, reflecting the 4-vCPU scale, with 6,896.97 on stress-ng multi-core and 5,733.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory operations register in lower benchmark tiers, which bounds performance on memory-bandwidth-intensive processing. However, small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 418.9 GB/sec, supporting standard transactional demands such as Redis operations at 7.58 million sets per second and static web serving at 14.39 GB/sec.

This hardware balance makes the n4d-standard-4 cost-efficient for general-purpose applications that leverage strong single-thread IPC without requiring dedicated GPUs or high-throughput local disk storage. Typical operational fits include web serving tiers, application backends, API gateways, microservices, and moderate database workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor and 16 GB of memory. It features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the n4d-standard-4 delivers top-tier single-threaded performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, while multi-core workloads, web serving throughput, and in-memory key-value processing place consistently in average percentiles. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck relative to its high single-core execution rates. With its balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory configuration, the n4d-standard-4 is well structured for standard application hosting, microservices, and general cloud workloads that benefit from high per-core execution speeds.
